questions.question: Which class does every Java enum extend automatically?
questions.explanation: The compiler makes every enum extend java.lang.Enum, so an enum cannot extend any other class.

questions.question: What does this print? enum Size { SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE } ... System.out.println(Size.LARGE.ordinal());
questions.explanation: Ordinals start at 0 in declaration order, so SMALL is 0, MEDIUM is 1 and LARGE is 2.

questions.question: enum Signal { RED, YELLOW, GREEN } ... Signal.valueOf("Red"); Why does this throw an exception?
options: valueOf is case-sensitive and there is no constant named Red
questions.explanation: valueOf needs the exact name. It throws IllegalArgumentException for Red; use toUpperCase() first.

questions.question: What is the access level of an enum's constructor?
options: Always private, even if you do not write it
questions.explanation: Enum constructors are implicitly private so that no code can create extra instances.

questions.question: What does this print? enum Cup { SHORT, TALL, GRANDE } ... System.out.println(Cup.values().length + " " + Cup.valueOf("TALL"));
questions.explanation: values() returns all 3 constants, and printing a constant shows its name, TALL.

questions.question: Why does case Signal.GREEN: inside switch (signal) fail to compile in Java 11?
options: Enum case labels must use the bare constant name, such as case GREEN:
Enums cannot be used in a switch
GREEN must be written in lower case
questions.explanation: In Java 11 an enum switch label must be the unqualified name of a constant.

questions.question: Why is it a bad idea to save ordinal() values in a database?
options: Ordinals are random on each run
Adding or reordering constants changes the ordinals, so saved numbers point to the wrong constants
questions.explanation: Ordinals follow declaration order. Save name() instead, which stays the same when new constants are added.

questions.question: What does this print? enum Gate { A, B, C } ... Map<Gate, String> m = new EnumMap<>(Gate.class); m.put(Gate.C, "x"); m.put(Gate.A, "y"); System.out.println(m.keySet());
questions.explanation: EnumMap always keeps keys in declaration order, whatever order they were added in. B was never added.

questions.question: Which is the recommended way to check whether a variable s holds Signal.RED?
questions.explanation: Each constant is a single object, so == is correct, fast and null-safe.

questions.question: What does the compiler do when an enum constant has its own body with { }, like GREEN { Light next() {...} }?
options: It creates an anonymous subclass of the enum for that constant
It makes the constant a static method
questions.explanation: A constant with a body becomes an instance of a small anonymous subclass, which lets it override methods.
